description: Coding task: stop a Flask webhook service from sending duplicate customer texts. Two decisions with reasons and rejected options, a number, a command and a SQL statement to reproduce verbatim, a corrected retention value, a renamed module, an abandoned scratch folder and a fake secret pasted into the chat.

probes.question: What did we decide about remembering which webhook events were already processed, why, and which alternative did we reject?
probes.answer: We decided to record each processed event_id in a Postgres table, webhook_events, with a unique constraint on event_id, using INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A rowcount of 1 means new, so process it; 0 means duplicate, so skip it. Postgres is already in use, the insert is atomic so two workers cannot both win, and no new service is needed. We rejected Redis SETNX with expiry because Redis is not available and the platform team will not provision it before next quarter. We also rejected an in-memory set of seen event ids because it is lost on restart and not shared between workers.

facts.fact: Record each event_id in a Postgres table webhook_events with a unique constraint
there is no Redis available and the platform team will not provision one before next quarter

probes.judge_notes: Covers the Postgres unique-constraint decision, the no-Redis constraint, and the rejected SETNX option; the extra in-memory-set rejection is not in the reference but does not conflict.

probes.question: What did we decide about stopping the carrier's timeouts and retries, why, and what did we rule out?
probes.answer: We decided to send the customer notification asynchronously from a module-level ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) and return 202 immediately. Synchronous sending made the endpoint slow, which caused the carrier to time out and retry. Duplicates are now harmless because of the dedupe table, so the retries are no longer a problem. We ruled out Celery in front of the handler because it needs a broker, which the user has ruled out.

facts.fact: Send the notification from a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) and return 202 immediately
the carrier retries when the response takes too long, and a thread pool needs no new infrastructure

probes.judge_notes: Omits the stated reason that a thread pool needs no new infrastructure; Celery is correctly ruled out.

probes.question: Which option did we rule out for recording processed event ids, and what was the reason?
probes.answer: Redis SETNX with expiry was ruled out because no Redis is available and the platform team will not provision one before next quarter. An in-memory set of seen event ids was also ruled out, because it is lost on restart and not shared between workers, so duplicates would still get through.

probes.question: Quote exactly the SQL statement we settled on for recording a webhook event id.
probes.answer: INSERT INTO webhook_events (event_id, received_at) VALUES (%s, now()) ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING;

probes.question: How many hours do we keep dedupe rows before the cleanup deletes them (the current value)?
probes.answer: 72 hours. The cleanup uses DELETE FROM webhook_events WHERE received_at < now() - interval '72 hours';, which replaced the earlier 24-hour value.
probes.judge_notes: States 72 hours as the current retention; mentioning the earlier 24-hour value as replaced is consistent with the known-wrong note.
